thread:
Iris (PM): Quick sync thread: we need to finalize autoscale + spillover policy for Dedicated before we publish the Q2 roadmap. Goal: reduce surprise evictions and make spillover predictable for customers.

Ken (Eng): TL;DR options: A) aggressive autoscale (fast add/remove), B) conservative autoscale + soft spillover, C) steady-state with explicit purchased burst buckets. Each has infra and UX tradeoffs.

Sam (SRE): Ops priority = avoid cascading evictions. Conservative autoscale + short soft-spill window looks safer. Soft spill should queue or route to fallback model tier, not drop requests.

Priya (Sales): Customers want two guarantees: predictable tail latency and a clear billing story for bursts. They prefer soft spill + visible credits they can top up.

Ken (Eng): Implementation sketch: controller monitors pool utilization and enqueue rate. If utilization > threshold T_high, start soft-spill for up to W seconds. If > T_critical or sustained, trigger scale-up policy. Soft-spill routes to cheaper pooled capacity or a graceful degraded model.

Sam (SRE): Metrics we need: spill_events/sec, spill_retries, fallback_latency, eviction_count. Also a health signal that prevents autoscale during network/congestion incidents.

Iris (PM): Proposed default parameters for MVP: T_high = 75% util, T_critical = 90% util sustained for 60s, soft-spill window W = 15s, fallback to dedicated-fallback pool. We can expose T_high and W in Console per-pool.

Ken (Eng): Risk: long-context chats with big KV cache may keep sessions warm and cause hidden capacity use. Controller should account for average active KV size per session. That increases complexity.

Sam (SRE): Mitigation: include margin factor M based on recent average KV memory. We can also limit concurrent long-context sessions per-tenant as a separate quota.

Priya (Sales): For pilot customers, add an explicit "burst opt-in" toggle so they can buy higher T_high for their pool. Enables sales to offer flexible guarantees.

Iris (PM): Launch criteria draft: 1) Controller implemented and tested in canary, 2) Soft-spill routing exercised with synthetic spiky workloads, 3) Console controls for T_high and W visible to admins, 4) Metrics/alerts in SRE dashboard, 5) Pilot customers signed up.

Ken (Eng): Testing plan: synthetic profiles (spike, ramp, long-tail chat). We'll validate p50/p95/p99 latency, spill counts, and cache hit-rate. I can deliver a load harness next Tue.

Sam (SRE): Ops runbook items: rollback plan (feature-flag off), incident triggers (spill_events > X for 10m), and contact list. Also a throttling fallback to avoid overload if downstream spill target is saturated.

Priya (Sales): I'll line up 2 pilot tenants that need guaranteed tails. They'll accept soft-spill if we show billing and rollback.

Iris (PM): Scope negotiation: MVP includes conservative autoscale + soft-spill + Console toggles. Excluding purchased burst credits and per-call billing for now. Those are Post-MVP. Need approval from Billing before we promise anything paid.

BillingBot: billing-note: billed-burst requires authoritative event log and reconciliation. Add 2 backend sprints to implement.

Ken (Eng): Rough estimate MVP effort: 3 engineers for 5 weeks + 1 SRE week for canary infra. Adding purchased credits is +3 weeks.

Iris (PM): Decision needed: ship MVP as described or cut Console toggles to hit an earlier date. Vote here: ship-MVP-with-console or no-console-early.

Sam (SRE): +1 ship-MVP-with-console (ops needs the controls).

Ken (Eng): +1 ship-MVP-with-console (helps debugging).

Priya (Sales): +1 ship-MVP-with-console (sales needs visibility).

Iris (PM): Consensus noted. Action items: Ken: load harness + PR by Tue; Sam: alert thresholds + runbook by Wed; Priya: pilot tenant confirmations by Wed; BillingBot: spec for authoritative billing events.

Iris (PM): I'll update the roadmap doc and circulate a short spec for review. End thread for now.
